鉢巻.name: Hachimaki
鉢巻.desc: A unique shop in the Koza streetscape with two faces: a soba shop by day and "Bar Samurai" by night (* it may have closed as of 2026). Look for the red gate and the words NEW YORK RESTAURANT. A gentle, light pork-bone soup and rare thin, wavy noodles.
t: * As of July 2026 it may have closed, so please be aware.
On this Okinawa soba journey, I'll introduce "Hachimaki" in Chuo, Okinawa City. I went to eat here in May 2025 😄

I visited "Hachimaki," in the streetscape of Koza in Chuo, Okinawa City. The exterior is quite unique: a gate like a red torii with the words "NEW YORK RESTAURANT," and red paper lanterns and decorations reading "Sakaba (tavern)" hanging from it, giving off a rather mysterious atmosphere 😊
Hachimaki (a unique exterior with a red gate as its landmark)

No wonder, since this shop actually also operates as a bar by night, under the name "Samurai (Bar Samurai)." Looking at the banners, as the soba shop "Hachimaki" it's open 11:00 am to 3:00 pm and 5:00 pm to 10:00 pm, and as the night bar "Samurai" from 10:00 pm to 5:00 am, truly a shop with two faces, day and night 🍶
Two faces: the soba shop "Hachimaki" by day, and Bar "Samurai" by night
Okinawa soba made by Otō (Dad)  Large ¥950  Medium ¥850

Inside, it's built just like a bar, with corrugated metal walls, a tapestry of a samurai under the moon, and red, pink, and green paper lanterns hanging, creating a unique world. There's a sofa seating area too, so it feels less like a daytime Okinawa soba shop and more like visiting a nighttime establishment 😅 There was even a sign saying "Weekdays only: karaoke, all-you-can-sing ¥500," which clearly conveys that nights are the main business.
Counter seats inside (with a sign for weekday-only all-you-can-sing karaoke ¥500)
The tapestry of the samurai under the moon and the paper lanterns create a unique world
There's sofa seating too, giving a nighttime-bar atmosphere
A samurai suit of armor is displayed too. As expected of Bar "Samurai"

Honestly, my impression is that Okinawa soba shops that are open at night often have strongly seasoned flavors, probably with a finishing bowl in mind. So I thought this one would be that kind too, but in a good way my expectations were betrayed.

Now, let's look at the menu. Okinawa soba (medium) ¥850, (large) ¥950, tebichi (pig's feet) soba ¥1,000, sets with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice), and even jushi taco rice. This time I went with the classic and ordered the "Okinawa soba (large)" 🍜
Menu at the shop front
Menu (you can choose between wavy noodles and flat noodles)
Drink menu (a wide selection of awamori and sours too. You can tell nights are the main business)

And what's interesting is that you can choose the noodles from "wavy noodles" and "flat noodles." Since I was there, I asked the staff member for a recommendation, and they pushed the wavy noodles, so I obediently chose the wavy noodles.
After a while, the Okinawa soba (large) appeared! Topped with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), egg, fish cake (kamaboko), and green onions, it's a very standard-looking bowl 😄
Okinawa soba (large)  ¥950

First, the soup. Mm, this is pork-bone based, but only a faint pork-bone flavor, a very gentle taste. Since it's a shop that's also open at night, I had braced myself for a strong flavor, so this was a welcome surprise. It's light and goes down smoothly.

Next, the noodles. The wavy noodles I chose are actually quite rare. I don't remember seeing thin, wavy noodles much in Okinawa soba. And they're finished soft. Since the soup is gentle, these thin wavy noodles seem to cling to it nicely.
Rare thin, wavy noodles. Finished on the soft side

Looking at the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) topping, the flavor has soaked in moderately, which is nice. However, some parts still had a bit of sinewy texture. The egg and fish cake are the usual reliable supporting players.

Overall, in contrast to its unique appearance as a nighttime bar, "Hachimaki"'s Okinawa soba was a gentle, light, and, in a good way, ordinary bowl. The novelty of thin, wavy noodles was a small discovery 😊
Rating (9/15): While sightseeing in Koza, why not stop by "Hachimaki (Samurai)" and enjoy its two faces: Okinawa soba by day and a bar by night? 👋

マルヨ製麺（沖縄市）.name: Maruyo Seimen (Okinawa City)
マルヨ製麺（沖縄市）.desc: A shop run directly by a noodle factory near Kensō (Okinawa Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park). The chewy in-house fresh noodles made with Okinawa-grown wheat are high-level, and the top pick is the "Yokubari Soba," topped with a whole-rib bone-in pork rib (hon-soki), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku).
t: I ate here in September 2023 😁
Maruyo Seimen

This shop is relatively close to Kensō (Okinawa Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park), but when I googled it, it seems to have shops in various places (;^ω^) This time, as usual without any research, I happened to find this place and went in.
The menu in front of the entrance
Looking at the menu sign in front of the shop entrance, the "Yokubari Soba" is introduced as the "shop's top pick."

It's described as "a luxurious dish topped with a bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) using one whole pork rib, soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku)." So my order is decided: this "shop's top pick, Yokubari Soba" 😊

It was lunchtime, but probably because it was a weekday, the shop was empty. Entering from the entrance, there's a ticket machine (cash only) near the entrance, and I bought the recommended "Yokubari Soba (medium)" and ordered it from a staff member.
On the table was a laminated sheet explaining what seem to be this shop's selling points, the "fresh noodles" and the "broth."

The explanation says, "Fresh noodles: chewy texture, smooth slurping, made with Okinawa-grown wheat" and "Broth: light yet rich and savory, a luxurious broth of seafood, chicken, and pork, superb with the in-house fresh noodles." Just reading the explanation makes it sound delicious 😋
After a while, the "Yokubari Soba" came.
Yokubari Soba, medium  ¥900

First, the soup 🤗 According to the explanation it's a blended broth of seafood, chicken, and pork, and since "seafood" came first, I assumed on my own that the bonito base would be strong and took a sip.
But the taste was somehow different from what I imagined? I took another sip to check. Again, it didn't seem like a bonito base? If anything, it felt like a chicken and pork base.
It's a tasty soup, but personally I would have liked a stronger seafood feel (;^ω^) But it's still ordinarily tasty.
Next, the fresh noodles. They're medium-thick straight noodles, and as described, they have a chewy texture, moderate springiness, and are smooth. Delicious noodles 😊
Is that something made from Okinawa-grown wheat kneaded into the noodles? You can see something worked into them.
The noodles Maruyo Seimen is proud of. You can tell the smooth, chewy feel even from the photo.

Rating (9.5/15): It's ordinarily tasty. I thought the fresh noodles in particular are high-level. I thought they're similar to and as high-level as "Kinchichi Soba" that I ate in Onna Village and "Suke Soba" that I ate in Ginowan City the other day. The soup is delicious and goes with the noodles, but personally I thought a stronger seafood style would be better. The toppings are tender but lightly flavored, so personally I'd prefer them to be more flavor-soaked. Why not try the fresh noodles made with Okinawa-grown wheat at least once?
